newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia seeks new investors for Inmet zinc mine.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia seeks new investors for Inmet zinc mine.

text.p: Tunisia is seeking new investors for a zinc and lead mine closed in October by Inmet Mining Corp because of falling world zinc prices, the Tunisian Industry Minister said.
"The ministry is seeking a foreign investor and we are keeping the Bougrine mine ready to resume production," Slaheddine Bouguerra told parliament late on Thursday.
In October Inmet shut down the northwestern Bougrine mine, originally developed by Toronto-based Metall Mining Corp.
"We had proposed to Inmet to give up the Bougrine mine for a symbolic dinar and that the Tunisian banks write down the mine's debts, in an attempt to keep the mine working," Bouguerra said.
Bouguerra said the mine was shut because its profitability was calculated on the basis of a zinc price of $1,250 per tonne. World prices are now around $1,000.
He said the mine's cumulative losses were 70 million dinars ($70 million) and its workforce of 400 had been cut to a maintenance staff of 30.
Tunisia produced 49,700 tonnes of zinc during the first seven months of 1996, officials statistics showed.
Zinc production had increased sharply in 1995, with output of 80,600 tonnes against 26,600 tonnes in 1994 and 2,400 tonnes in 1993.
Tunisia also produced 6,000 tonnes of lead during the first seven months of 1996. Total production of lead was 11,300 tonnes in 1995, up from 4,600 tonnes in 1994.
